text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST

- State Department accuses aide to Israeli prime minister of being disrespectful to President Bill Clinton by referring to U.S. statements about Jewish settlements as "semantic posturing". The aide, David Bar-Illan, denies having used term.
- Alternative to cuts in child allowances could be announced today.
- Israeli President Ezer Weizman: I can't sleep well at night because of concern over country's situation.
- Former Justice Minister Yaacov Neeman indicted.
- Israeli Labour party leader Shimon Peres: Prime Minister Netanyahu, Shin Bet security services in crisis.
- Netanyahu: Privatisation plan complete. Prime minister approves new aid package for development zones.
- Union Bank of Switzerland upgrades Bank Leumi to "buy".
- Rabbi Shlomo Lorenz, chairman of Bank of Israel's advisory council, tells members of Knesset finance committee: Don't shackle Bank of Israel Governor Jacob Frenkel.
GLOBES
- Ministers of finance and trade and industry adopt majority of commission recommendations to encourage industry in development zones.
- Knesset approves budget rise of 28 percent -- for itself.
HAARETZ
-Israeli Ambassador to U.S.: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat will harden stances in negotiations after what Clinton said about settlements.
- Foreign ministry not distributing prime minister's office document on violations from the Palestinian side.
- Israeli army: The Palestinians intend to house 600 freed prisoners in the Hebron casbah.
- CIA received information in 1992 of a planned attack on the Israeli embassy in Argentina and did nothing.
- Numbers studying in institutions for newly religious Jews up in the last six months by 28 percent -- most significant rise among girls.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Building of Jewish neighbourhood in East Jerusalem to be frozen. This to be the advice of Netanyahu to his interior minister.
- Poll shows only 27 percent of Israelis smoke.
- Exemptions from company tax for two years on investments in "A" development areas.
MAARIV

- Israel: American criticism won't dictate our way of life. High Court of Justice approves resumption of building on Efrat's Givat Hazayit, Olive Hill. Sources in Jerusalem: A meeting soon between Netanyahu and Arafat.
